result.document_summary: Los Angeles Housing Department relocation assistance bulletins (effective July 1, 2026) describing no-fault eviction grounds, relocation payment amounts and procedures under the RSO and JCO, and enhanced relocation for demolition for new construction under the Resident Protections Ordinance.
result.notes: Both bulletins concern no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO, so the rules fall under just_cause_eviction. The bulletins do not state the RSO/JCO coverage criteria (building age, unit count) in testable terms, so coverage is left as the general tenancy condition. Two rules are recorded: the no-fault eviction/relocation regime and the RPO demolition relocation regime. The B bulletin fee chart is headed 'Effective July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026' while the document is Rev 07.01.2026 and its A bulletin lists the same fee amounts for 2026-27; fee amounts were not extracted as separate rules since they are administrative fees paid by landlords to the city.

rules.title: No-fault eviction relocation assistance and filing requirements (RSO/JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords evicting for a tenant-not-at-fault reason (owner/relative occupancy, demolition, removal from rental use, government order to vacate, etc.) must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice, file a copy of the notice within 3 days, and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of serving the notice. Amounts depend on tenant status and tenancy length, with a one-month's-rent amount for qualifying natural-person-owned single-family dwellings under the JCO.
rules.key_value: $11,000 / $14,400 (eligible, <3 yrs / 3+ yrs or low income); $23,150 / $27,400 (qualified); one month's rent for qualifying JCO single-family dwellings
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in the City of Los Angeles.

all_of.value: unit subject to the RSO or JCO
all_of.text: units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)

exemptions.label: Resident manager replaced by another resident manager

all_of.value: evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager
all_of.text: Evicting a resident manager to replace him/her with another resident manager

all_of.value: required to evict due to natural disaster hazard not caused by landlord negligence
all_of.text: required to evict due to hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster, not caused by the landlord's negligence

rules.exemptions_text: No relocation assistance is owed when evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager, or when eviction is required by natural-disaster hazards not caused by landlord negligence; Mom and Pop owners (four or fewer units) pay reduced amounts for owner/relative occupancy evictions; accumulated rent may be offset against relocation assistance except for government-ordered vacates.
rules.interaction: Demolition for new construction of Protected Units is governed instead by the Resident Protections Ordinance and the state Housing Crisis Act; Ellis Act provisions (LAMC 151.22-151.28) apply to RSO units withdrawn from rental use.
yields_to: Resident Protections Ordinance (for demolition of Protected Units for new construction)
California Housing Crisis Act (Gov. Code § 66300 et seq.)

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition for new construction
rules.requirement: Owners demolishing Protected Units for new construction must pay relocation assistance at the higher of state (Housing Crisis Act) or city amounts; lower-income households receive enhanced standardized payments, and all other tenants receive the RSO/JCO amounts. Owners choose one of three relocation options and face penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit for noncompliance.
rules.key_value: $115,480 (extremely low), $96,750 (very low), $87,450 (low income) per household; RSO/JCO Chart A amounts for households above low income
rules.citation: L.A. Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance); Cal. Gov. Code § 66300 et seq.
rules.quoted_span: City laws require all tenants be paid relocation assistance in the amounts required by the RSO or JCO within 15 days of serving a notice to terminate tenancy, which must be enhanced for lower income tenants if the project is subject to the Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO), effective 2/11/2025
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units (including all RSO units, units with affordability covenants or rent control in the past five years, units rented by lower-income households in the past five years, and units withdrawn under the Ellis Act in the past 10 years) that will be demolished for new construction.

all_of.value: Protected Unit demolished for new construction
all_of.text: Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction

rules.interaction: Relocation must be at the higher of state Housing Crisis Act or city law amounts; payment above the RSO/JCO amount under Option 3 is regulated by state law. If units are not Protected Units or not occupied by lower-income tenants, regular RSO/JCO relocation rules apply.
yields_to: California Housing Crisis Act (Gov. Code § 66300 et seq.) where its amounts are higher
